q-49136:
Recall that

$$
\int \frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=\text{arcsec}\,x.
$$

Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x)=\int {f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x-\int 3\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x-3\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\text{ arcsec }x-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-71768:
Recall that 

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=\int {f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (5{x}^{4}+\frac{7}{1+{x}^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\int 5{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{7}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int {x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+7\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\cdot \frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+7\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C \\  & ={x}^{5}+7\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-50136:
First, we rearrange the equation to isolate the derivative term:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-4{e}^{2x}-2x.
$$

Then, we integrate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-4{e}^{2x}-2x)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\int (-4{e}^{2x}-2x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}y & =\int (-4{e}^{2x}-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-4\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x-2\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2{e}^{2x}-{x}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
